title: Backing Bessie, Clara, Mamie and Trixie Smith at the Howard
summary: Four or five shows a day, with blues singers as headliners who brought their own comedians and chorus girls but usually only a pianist.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: How many shows a day were you doing?

Aw, man! Let's see. Four or five a day, and it all depends on what they have in there. They had a blues singer in there, you know, one of the Smiths, Bessie Smith, Mamie Smith, but mainly Bessie, and Clara. Clara wasn't bad. She was very good. Trixie Smith. I played for all of them.
Was it usually a blues singer who was the headliner?
Yes. Yes, back then, yes, because they would come in and bring their own show, you know, see,
and comedians, so many chorus girls, and whatnot.
When they brought their own show didn't they bring their own musicians too?
No. Well, maybe a pianist, because -- and he would sit down and tell you what we want, this is the way we do it, such-and-such-and-such. You know?
